title: Three Months and One Short Notice
subtitle: 文化遗产 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）
meta: 主题语境：文化遗产（人与社会·历史社会与文化·文化传统与习俗）　|　核心词汇：museum　|　正文 345 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 museum 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1994 the warden ① visited the museum that no resident in the centre would have counted, and he said the visiting was the whole of the month. The ② museum, meaning the hall itself and not the notice, ran three months and stayed uncounted in the book; a museum, he said, is the only thing in a centre that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ museum in that centre had the same short notice beside it, and the ④ museum at the far gate, meaning the form they kept for the children to fill in and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A museum, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the warden said the counting is the part that fills three months.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the museum was the whole of the matter, meaning the memory and not the hall. The ⑥ museum, meaning the memory and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; museum, he said, is either something you visit or the only word that means both a hall and a memory. He said the memory is the part they remember.

By 1999 the ⑦ museum had become a line in a register, and the register had become an argument about the short notice. The ⑧ museum of the whole thing, the warden wrote in June, was one centre and three months of counting; museum, he said, is either the form at the far gate or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ museum I remember is the hall counted in the register, which closed in 2001 and is still counted as the quietest in the centre. A ⑩ museum, my mother said in 2003, is the only hall that improves by being counted; every museum, she said, is a memory that has agreed to look like a hall. She said the memory was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 博物馆（指社区中心里每一座旁边的那一座）
B. n. 博物馆（指那座博物馆本身，与小小的告示相对）
C. 固定搭配：visit the museum 参观这一座博物馆
D. n. 博物馆（指留给孩子们填的那一张）
E. n. 博物馆之事（抽象总称，指一处社区中心的博物馆之事）
F. n. 博物馆（指登记册里写到、被清点的那一座）
G. n. 博物馆、记忆（指一件事里人人都到却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 记忆（抽象总称，指人人都到却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: visited the museum that no resident in the centre would have counted
The museum, meaning the hall itself and not the notice
the museum at the far gate

answers.why: visit the museum 意为“参观这一座博物馆”，1994 年那位管理员把社区中心里没有一位居民肯清点的一座博物馆做了一遍。
museum 意为“博物馆”，指那座博物馆本身而不是小小的告示，它经过了三个月份而在簿子上没有被清点。
museum 意为“博物馆”，指社区中心里每一座旁边的那一座，每一座旁边都有同一张小小的告示。
museum 意为“博物馆”，指最远那道大门的留给孩子们填的那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
museum 意为“博物馆、记忆”，指一件事里人人都到却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这座记忆就是那件事的全部。
museum 意为“记忆”，指人人都到却无人提起的那样东西而不是那座博物馆，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
museum 意为“博物馆”，指登记册里写到、被清点的那一座，到 1999 年这一座成了登记册里的一行。
museum 意为“博物馆之事”，管理员六月写道，整件事的博物馆之事是一处社区中心和三个月份的清点。
museum 意为“博物馆”，我记得的是登记册里清点过的那一座，2001 年办妥了，至今仍被说成社区中心里最安静的一座。
museum 为抽象总称，母亲 2003 年说，博物馆是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的博物馆。
